lesson.grammar_point: modal verbs of obligation and advice

listenings.text: Hey, about Sunday. I want to warn you about a couple of things before you say yes. We have to leave at six in the morning, which is brutal, and the bus does not wait, so we really must be there on time. You do not have to bring food, because there is a place at the top, but honestly you should bring your own water. It is expensive up there and the queue is strict, one bottle per person. Oh, and you must not wear new shoes. My cousin did that last year on purpose because they looked good in photos and she could not walk for three days. Tell me tonight, because I have to confirm the seats.

Ana, quick one before the call. I have just read the new guidelines and there are two things you should know. First, we must not change the logo colour, not even a little. That one is not negotiable and the main stakeholder checks it personally. Second, we do not have to use their font in social posts, which everybody assumes we do, so that is good news for the campaign. My advice is that we should send them the layouts on Thursday instead of Friday. If they see it early, they can ask for small changes instead of big ones. You do not have to decide now, but let me know before the call.

extra_audio.text: Hugo explains that guests have to leave the keys in the box downstairs. Ana asks him if she has to take the rubbish out every day. Hugo answers that she does not have to, but that she should do it on Tuesday nights. Ana asks whether she can invite two friends over. Hugo warns her that she must not have parties, because the neighbours are strict about noise.

reading.rtitle: House Rules -- The Flat in Lisbon
paras: Welcome. You do not have to read all of this, but you should read the first two lines, because everybody asks me the same questions anyway.
Keys: you have to leave them in the metal box downstairs when you go, and you must not take them with you to the airport. Somebody did that in March and it cost us both a very long afternoon.

Noise: the neighbours are strict. You can have friends over, but you must not have parties, and after eleven at night you should keep the windows closed. The rubbish goes out on Tuesday nights, and you do not have to do it every day.

The rest is easy. You do not have to clean before you leave, we do that. You can use everything in the kitchen. If something breaks, you should message me instead of trying to fix it on purpose, because the last guest tried and now there are two things broken.
reading.source: Message from Hugo, the host -- Lisbon
